key_insight: VASPO combines a critic and a self-teacher at the same student-generated prefixes, using privileged value estimation plus bounded self-distillation to improve reasoning-policy updates.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical PPO-style training recipe for reasoning models that leverages privileged information more effectively than prior GRPO-based self-distillation schemes.
method: Critic predicts continuation returns and forms token-level PPO advantages at student prefixes.
Self-teacher uses the same privileged information to scale selected positive advantages with bounded probability ratios.
Design exploits complementary dynamics: critic is stronger near the end of responses, while teacher guidance is strongest early and late.
evidence_signal: Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VASPO improves mean accuracy over PPO by 2.59 points on Qwen3-4B and 1.81 points on OLMo3-7B, with the best mean accuracy on Knights and Knaves.
watch_item: Because the method depends on privileged information and careful advantage/ration coupling, implementation stability and reproducibility may be sensitive to how those signals are estimated and bounded.
paper_title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
